Nowadays, using artificial intelligence and advanced resource computational, it is possible to obtain models data-driven, combining mathematical algorithms that optimize the management of the life cycle and prognostic the state of health. The Gaussian process regression algorithm is proposed to develop a model and validate it in another dataset, it guarantees the performance, reliability, and safety of the battery. For the verification stage, the lithium-ion battery dataset of the NASA research repository was used, and to ensure the effectiveness of the model, the dataset was separated into 30% for the training and 70% for the testing during the research. For the validation stage was added a noise, two datasets were used, and compared their results using metrics quantitative. The experimental showed results R2 > 98% and MAE and RMSE < 0.02 these confirmed that the proposed methodology demonstrates high prediction accuracy of the proposed in practice.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Peruvian National Network, a model for use in the health sector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE XXIX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The Peruvian government has a National Fiber Backbone Network that has been operating for 5 years, network that connects Lima, the capital of Peru, with 180 provincial capitals, which only uses less than 5% of its operating capacity. On the other hand, health entities currently use very low connectivity capacity with an average of 21.2 Mbps, which is insufficient to provide efficient and quality health care. Likewise, the Peruvian government pays an average of 20 dollars per Mbps for the connectivity of its health entities in the provinces. The authors propose to overcome this critical situation by making use of the Dorsal Network based on Executive Directorial Resolution No. 245-2021-MTC/24, which establishes zero cost for State communications in the Backbone Network. In addition, corporate purchases should be made throughout the health sector. If the measures recommended by the authors are implemented, the price of the Internet for the State would pay, in the best-case scenario, only 8.75% of the current price. This would allow the Peruvian State in the health sector to have greater connectivity equivalent to that of developed countries.

articleTitle: Mobile Application for the Timely Detection of Potential COVID-19 Infections
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE XXIX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The objective of this study is to determine user acceptance of a mobile application for the timely detection of possible COVID-19 infections in the city of Cajamarca. For this purpose, the mobile application Covid Alerta (Covid Alert) was developed for devices with the Android operating system. The OpenUp software development methodology was used for the development of this application. The applied, quantitative, exploratory research used 2 survey forms: one to measure how the detection of COVID-19 was carried out in the city of Cajamarca, and another to measure the impact of using a mobile application to detect infected contacts. The results indicated that the most reliable screening tests are molecular tests; in addition, 85% of respondents felt much safer receiving alerts of infected contacts on their mobile devices. Likewise, 88.5% indicated confidently that the application complies with registering and reporting infected contacts. This shows that 88.8% of users accepted the use of mobile applications for the timely detection of possible COVID-19 infections.

articleTitle: Coefficients search for a regression curve of a neonatal incubator using evolutionary computing techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE XXIX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: A regression model to correct temperature readings of an infrared sensor has been implemented, the target was to predict the known inner object temperature readings using the infrared temperature readings of the object’s surface, the infrared sensor die temperatures and light intensity data collected from a 35 hour experiment with the object lying inside a neonatal incubator. We have applied different evolutionary computing techniques like Genetic Algorithms (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Differential Evolution (DE), to obtain the best fit to the data and in this way correct the temperature reading. The best prediction was achieved with differential evolution with a mean square error metric of 0.044404 followed by 0.044410 obtained with PSO and 0.046037 with GA. Also, with the best results obtained, the error was calculated considering the measured light intensity signal to see if this variable helps to further decrease the error.

Author Keywords: Differential Evolution and non contact temperature measurement
